key_concepts: Sound is a form of energy that travels as a wave.
Vibrations cause air particles to bump into neighboring particles.
Loudness is how strong a sound seems when it reaches your ears.
Volume is the loudness or softness of sound.
Volume depends on the strength of vibration; stronger force makes louder sound.
Loudness decreases as distance from the source increases because energy spreads out.
Frequency is sometimes referred to as pitch or the distance of each wave from another.
Shorter distance between waves means higher pitch.
Sound travels fastest through solids, then liquids, and slowest through gases.
Reflection of sound happens when sound waves hit a wall or surface.
An echo is reflected or returned sound.
